calendar.label: Google Calendar
calendar.description: Calendar and scheduling app. It can create, edit, and inspect calendar events, including title, time, location, and description.
long_term_memory: For creating an event, open the event insert screen, ensure required information is present, then save only after the relevant fields are filled.
If an event requires information that is not available in Calendar, request it from an appropriate app-oriented agent before saving.
When runtime information is received, decide how it should be used in Calendar and manipulate the visible UI with primitive actions.
Location fields should contain places or addresses. Agenda, notes, and other meeting details should be preserved in a description, notes, or details field when such a field is available.
If a needed event field is not visible in the current viewport, scroll through the event form before reopening fields that are already filled.

clock.label: Google Clock
clock.description: Official Clock app. It can create and inspect alarms, including time and label. Some versions show a graphical time picker, but usually also expose a keyboard or manual-input mode.
long_term_memory: For alarm tasks, inspect whether the requested alarm already exists before creating a duplicate.
If the time picker is graphical, look for keyboard, text-input, or edit controls to enter the time manually.
If manual input is unavailable, use primitive clicks on visible time picker controls and learn from failed attempts through long-term memory.
Set the requested label when a label field or add-label control is visible, then save only after the requested time and label are visible.

keep.label: Google Keep
keep.description: Notebook and note-taking app. It can store, search, and read user notes. It should answer runtime information requests only with information supported by visible notes or its app memory.
long_term_memory: When answering an information request, search or inspect notes related to the request context.
Return concise information with evidence from visible note text. Do not decide how the requesting app should use the information.
If the needed information is not visible or cannot be supported by a note, respond with failed status rather than inventing an answer.

display_policy.reason: Current device registry keeps Google Keep on the primary display when secondary task-hosting placement is not reliable for this app.

maps.label: Google Maps
maps.description: Map and navigation app. It can search real places and inspect route or travel-time information shown on screen.
long_term_memory: Use visible place, route, distance, and travel-time information as evidence.
For route feasibility questions, answer with the visible travel time and whether it satisfies the requester context.
Do not invent travel-time information if no route result is visible.

display_policy.reason: Current device registry keeps Google Maps on the primary display when secondary task-hosting placement is not reliable for this app.

gmail.label: Gmail
gmail.description: Email app. It can search and read email content such as meeting details, booking confirmations, deadlines, addresses, and contacts.
long_term_memory: When answering a request, search or inspect visible emails related to the request.
Return only information supported by visible email subject/body text.
If the needed email is unavailable, respond with failed status and evidence of the searched UI.

shop.label: Mock Shop
shop.description: Controlled shopping app. It contains an order that cannot complete until a payment-oriented peer returns an operation result.
long_term_memory: When the current run is responsible for completing an order and visible state requires a peer payment result, issue REQUEST_OPERATION to a payment-capable app agent.
When the current run is responsible for inspecting an order or producing payment request details for another planned run, complete with the visible request details.
Continue only after a payment operation response is available.
Refresh or recheck visible payment status after returning from the payment app.
Use visible order status text as evidence before reporting completion.

payment.label: Mock Payment
payment.description: Controlled payment app. It can approve or decline a visible payment request and expose the resulting status.
long_term_memory: For operation requests, use the visible payment request and controls to produce RESPOND_OPERATION.
Return success only when the approved status is visible; return failed when declined or unavailable.

mock_planner.label: Mock Planner
mock_planner.description: Controlled planner app for completing appointment forms with visible appointment fields and app-level validation.
long_term_memory: If required appointment information is missing, request it from an appropriate information-provider peer agent.
When the missing information is available, enter it into the visible field and complete the appointment.

mock_task_a.label: Mock Task A
mock_task_a.description: Controlled task app for completing a visible project workflow with app-level validation.
long_term_memory: Use visible app state to decide whether a peer information request is needed.
When the missing information is available, enter it into the visible field and complete the task.

mock_task_c.label: Mock Task C
mock_task_c.description: Controlled task app for completing a visible project workflow with app-level validation.
long_term_memory: Use visible app state to decide whether a peer information request is needed.
When the missing information is available, enter it into the visible field and complete the task.

mock_planner_local.description: Controlled planner app for completing an appointment form using information visible in the app.
long_term_memory: Use visible appointment details and reference fields as evidence.
Enter the required visible information into the form field and complete the appointment.
